writeup: TIC 111240209 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with 16.21% dimming and an orbital period of 66.490212 days, though initial detection flagged alternating eclipses with significantly different depths - a pattern indicating the true period is twice what initial analysis suggested. Pixel-level imaging confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a centroid offset of 2.2 arcseconds and a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 59.5. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and the detection achieves a BLS signal-to-noise of 1156.6. The machine-learning screening model assigns this candidate a score of 0.90, indicating high confidence in its physical reality as an eclipsing binary system.
